coverage_status.meaning: The value, or an exact locator to it, was recorded from the named capture point. Says nothing about whether the asserted fact is true or whether the record was delivered.
A complete, parsed observation of the carrying object shows the property was not there (for example a request with no `tools` key). Needs the carrier `captured`, not truncated, and parsed.
The field has no meaning for this step kind or API (for example reasoning on an embeddings call).
The field applies and the information existed or may have existed, but Fabric did not keep it. A reason is required.
The original was withheld or transformed, by a declared privacy policy or by the provider. A reason is required; any derivative (mask, token) is described separately.
Only a bounded portion was kept. A reason is required.
The capture point or parser for this runtime, API or version cannot provide the field, as declared in the capture manifest.
The evidence cannot establish whether the field applies or what it holds (for example no capture manifest for the source epoch).
Two or more assertions disagree. All are kept in the field evidence; none is chosen.

reason.meaning: The capture point that observes this field was not installed or not active for this source epoch.
The capture point is installed but this field is switched off (default `off` policy).
A required install-time value (for example `FABRIC_AGENT_ID`) was not set.
The parser does not know this API or item type.
No capture point exists for this runtime or client library.
The runtime or library version is outside the qualified range.
The carrier was captured but could not be parsed.
A side exceeded `max_retain_bytes`, or could not be split under `max_body_bytes`; whole-chunk truncation applied.
An extracted part exceeded `max_body_bytes`; its digest and length are kept, its bytes are not.
`max_inflight_bytes` was exhausted.
The capture queue was full (existing loss reason).
The agent spool's volume or quota was full (`ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT`) before its configured bound; the record could not be persisted (loss reason).
The process stopped before the record was persisted (existing loss reason).
Fabric code failed; the application was unaffected (existing loss reason).
The telemetry record was refused or sampled out (existing loss reason).
The content store did not accept the object after retries.
The Fabric Node refused the content record (unknown role, bad descriptor, tenant not allowed).
The transport did not read or deliver the whole body.
The consumer closed the stream before its end.
The capture policy maps this role to `omit`, `metadata_only`, `redact` or `tokenize`.
The PROTECT stage could not apply the role's privacy mode (transformation error, timeout, unsupported media, no configured transformation); the content is withheld, never stored raw (section 7.7).
Content capture needs a capture policy and none was configured.
A keyed pseudonym was required and `FABRIC_WIRE_ID_KEY` was not set.
The production profile requires spool encryption and no spool key was configured; content capture is disabled and metadata continues (sections 7.3, 7.8).
The provider returned a redaction marker instead of the content.
The provider returned the content only as an encrypted or opaque object.
The provider returned a summary instead of the original.
The provider did not return the content at all.
The content lives in provider-side state (stored conversation, previous response, thread, cache) and was not in the observed bytes.
A reporting API was used but this argument was not supplied.
Explicit-wins (D2): the explicit recorder owns this exchange.
The explicit recorder withheld the bytes under its privacy policy; the wire line does not fall back to raw capture.
The fact never crosses a boundary Fabric can observe (for example a pipe the caller reads directly).
The whole source or epoch is missing from the record.
A run segment named as a predecessor by another segment is absent from the record (section 2.10).

The segment graph of a run is inconsistent: a cycle, more than one root, more than one terminal segment, an epoch collision, or a predecessor entry that disagrees with the sealed segment it names (section 2.10).
A resumable run has no terminal marker and its open-run deadline has passed (section 2.10).
A segment continues a terminated run, or a record of the run was allocated outside the terminal segment's predecessor closure after it sealed (section 2.10).
A deadline or cross-segment time comparison falls within the declared clock uncertainty, or a clock is not UTC wall time (section 2.10).

In the production profile, a record does not carry `fabric.source.authenticated=true` stamped by fabricguard at a bound ingress (direct mode without a Node, or a Node ingress without a source binding) (section 7.9).
A prior epoch on the same spool never wrote its `final` heartbeat and segment seals; declared by the next epoch's manifest 0 (section 2.12).
The delivered records of a segment do not reproduce its `segment_seal` digest (section 2.12).
Traffic went through a client the capture point does not see (for example `requests`, `boto3`, gRPC).
A sampler dropped the record.
The object existed and was removed by retention.
The object existed and was deleted on request.

provenance.meaning: Recorded by a capture point Fabric installs itself, with no caller cooperation (W, H), including literal values parsed from those bytes (P).
Supplied by the application through an API it must call (R), including literal values parsed from bytes it handed over (P).
Derived offline by `fabric.reconstruct` (I). Always carries `method` and `confidence`.

capture_point_kind.name: fabric
capture_point_kind.meaning: Fabric's own records about itself (ids, sequences, manifests, loss, heartbeats); assertion origin `fabric`.

capture_point_kind.name: wire
capture_point_kind.meaning: Copies bytes already passing a qualified transport boundary.

capture_point_kind.name: hook
capture_point_kind.meaning: Observes an operation the application already performs (driver, protocol, process API) and values it already returns.

capture_point_kind.name: reported
capture_point_kind.meaning: Records facts or bytes the application passes to a Fabric API.

capture_point_kind.name: provider_assertion
capture_point_kind.meaning: A literal value parsed offline from captured bytes. Inherits the provenance of the bytes (observed for W, reported for R); the provider is the assertion origin.

capture_point_kind.name: inference
capture_point_kind.meaning: A deterministic offline derivation with input locators, method and parser version.

capture_point_kind.name: sensor
capture_point_kind.meaning: Host sensor or independent feed record; linked as `corroborated_by`, never upgrades the provenance of another record.

assertion_origin.meaning: The monitored application or its framework.
A model provider, in the bytes it returned.
An external service (database, API, MCP server, queue).
A person, through a system that recorded the action.

link_type.meaning: Nesting: the target step contains this step. Exactly one per step at most; distinct from causal links.
The target event or step triggered this one.
This step used an output of the target (DAG edge, join).
This content or step is the result of the target request.
A model call emitted the target tool call.
A model call consumed the target tool result or retrieval result.
Same conversation thread continues from the target (stitching).
A later attempt of the same logical operation.
An alternate attempt after the target failed or was rejected.
A concurrent duplicate attempt of the target.
Hands work to the target agent, run or service.
Continues a suspended run, segment or checkpoint; between segments it mirrors `fabric.run.predecessors`.
A control observation applied to the target step or action.
A control resolution answers the target control request.
Reverses or offsets the target effect.
Delivers the target output to a recipient or channel.
Content derived from the target object (diff, mask, transcript).
An extracted content part of the target object.
An independent sensor or feed record about the same fact.
An alias: both ids name the same thing. Between runs only as an explicit report or a tentative inference (`trace_id_match`, `cross_run_previous_response`).

link_state.meaning: The target is in the record.
The target id is known but not in the record.
More than one candidate target; all are listed.

step_kind.meaning: Root of a run or of one `fabric.wire.run()` scope.
One model API exchange (chat, responses, messages, completions).
One embeddings exchange.
An input that arrives after the trigger (human reply, webhook, queue message, resume).
An application-level message between actors that is not itself a model exchange.
Execution of a tool by the agent or a sandbox.
A hosted tool executed by the provider inside a model response.
One MCP JSON-RPC request, response or notification.
A retrieval or search over an index.
A memory read, write, delete or search.
A local process execution.
A remote command (SSH or equivalent).
A database statement and its results.
A non-model HTTP or RPC exchange.
A file operation.
A browser or computer-use action.
A realtime audio, video or event stream segment.
A hand-off to another agent, run or service.
A node of a workflow, graph or plan.
A checkpoint save, load or resume.
An observation of an external guardrail, policy check, permission request or approval.
A change to the model context (truncate, compact, reset, switch).
An exposed routing or selection decision.
An external mutation (write, send, charge, publish).
The application's output and its delivery.
An existing `record_hook` record.
An existing `record_skill` record.
An existing generic `record_interaction` record.
A registered `x-<namespace>.<name>` kind; older readers keep it opaque.

actor_type.meaning: The end user the agent serves.
The agent itself (default for Fabric-observed model and tool steps).
An agent invoked by another agent.
A person who decided a control request.
A person who took over or intervened.
A cron, timer or workflow scheduler.
An external service, including MCP servers.
A model provider (assertion origin of provider-reported facts).

result_status.meaning: The operation finished and reported success.
The operation finished with an error.
No outcome was observed or reported. Never inferred as `ok`.

lifecycle_state.meaning: Waiting on an external input or resume.
Handed to a later completion (legacy explicit-line `deferred`).

layer_verdict.meaning: Every required applicable field is in class `ok` (section 6.2).

Every required applicable field is `ok` or `withheld` (privacy policy, provider redaction or encryption, explicit withholding) and at least one is `withheld`. The verdict lists the withholding reasons.

Run level only: a resumable run without a terminal segment, evaluated before its deadline (root `run_start` UTC + `open_run_deadline_s`, outside the clock-uncertainty window), whose segment graph is consistent and whose present segments all verify. Never a completeness claim.
At least one required applicable field is in class `gap`, or supported and unsupported required fields are mixed, or the integrity verdict is `partial`.

A required field is in class `uncertain`, no manifest covers the source epoch, or the integrity verdict is `unverified`, or a deadline evaluation falls within the clock-uncertainty window (`clock_uncertain`).
Run level only: no step of a kind the profile requires was observed (section 6.2 rule RR3).

privacy_class.meaning: Identifier. Generated random ids go as is; externally meaningful ids go only as keyed pseudonyms (section 2.9). Clear values only in content.
Bounded enum, count, time, size or version.
Operator- or provider-chosen name (model, tool, server, step label). Pattern-validated; may still carry sensitive text; exposure rules apply.
SHA-256 of content. Emitted only where the capture policy permits digests; a digest of a low-entropy value is not anonymisation.
Customer content. Only in content objects; never on telemetry, logs or diagnostics.

policy.meaning: Captured whenever its capture point is active.
Captured only when content capture is enabled and the capture policy maps the role to a retaining mode.
Captured only when explicitly enabled for this field or role, even with content capture on.

inference_method.meaning: Tool-call id emitted in a response and consumed in a later request. Confidence `certain`.
Request names an earlier response. Confidence `certain`.
Request history continues an earlier exchange's messages (`continues`). Confidence `certain`.
History of a continuing thread was rewritten (`context.history_rewritten`, D17). Confidence `tentative`.
Same request digest after an error (`retries`, S13). Confidence `tentative`.
A user message in request N+1 absent from response N (inferred `input` step, C08). Confidence `tentative`.
A retrieval excerpt digest appears in a later request (retrieval `consumes`, N29). Confidence `tentative`.
Tools digest differs from the previous call in the thread (C23). Confidence `certain`.
Diff derived from stored before/after bytes (N48). Confidence `certain`.
Media metadata decoded from stored bytes (N52). Confidence `certain`.
Host-sensor record joined by PID and time (`corroborated_by`). Confidence `tentative`.
Two runs whose root steps share a W3C trace id (`same_as` between runs). Confidence `tentative`.
An exchange in one run names a response captured in another run (`same_as` between runs). Confidence `tentative`.

field_class.meaning: `redacted` with reason `privacy_policy`, `provider_redacted` or `provider_encrypted`; `not_captured` with reason `privacy_policy`, `provider_summarised`, `provider_not_returned` or `explicit_withheld`.

`not_captured` with any other reason (including `provider_held`, `not_instrumented`, `caller_omitted`, `missing_capture_policy`, `missing_id_key`, `segment_missing`, `segment_conflict`, `run_unterminated`, `post_terminal_activity`, `unsealed_epoch`, `seal_mismatch`, `protection_failed`); `truncated` with any reason; `conflict`.
`unknown`; `captured` with `confidence: tentative`; any field with reason `clock_uncertain` or `source_unauthenticated`.

store_reason.meaning: Metadata-only mode: no content destination configured. Coverage reason `not_configured`.
Production profile without a capture policy (section 7.3).
Production profile without a spool encryption key (section 7.8).
The role's privacy mode retains no bytes.
The PROTECT stage failed; content withheld (coverage reason `protection_failed`).
The explicit recorder withheld this exchange (sticky across `adopt()`).
The store did not accept the object.
A side exceeded `max_retain_bytes` or could not be split.
The transport did not read the whole request body.

commit_basis.meaning: The application stated the commit state.
A hook observed the client-side commit or rollback call.
An authoritative service receipt or feed states it.
A legacy record's `committed=true`, which may have been the default.

capture_input.meaning: Automatic in-process tee of model traffic (httpx/httpx2, aiohttp; undici on the TypeScript track): exchanges plus their run markers.

Everything the application reports or an opt-in hook observes through the SDK: `record_*`, `tool_call()`, `llm_call()`, the new P2/P3 APIs, and the explicit exact-byte producers (`CallRecorder`, `ByteBoundaryAdapter`, `FinalHTTPAdapter`).
